# s287 — Gitignore the project lock file

`slicer init` lists `lock` in `.slicer/.gitignore`, and a project made before that gets the line the first time the lock file is created, so no project shows an untracked `.slicer/lock`.

**Findings:** s282 relay 2026-10-15: every write leaves `.slicer/lock` behind, and only `feedback.md` and `feedback-reported.json` are listed in `.slicer/.gitignore`, so a project other than this repo shows an untracked `.slicer/lock` after its first write · **Size:** S · **Tree:** slicer

**2026-10-15** — Verified: init lists lock in .slicer/.gitignore, after relay-runs.jsonl. Every lock acquisition (store.project_lock) adds the lock line if it is missing, best-effort: an unreadable or unwritable .slicer/.gitignore never blocks a write, while init stays strict. The spec triggered the line only on lock-file creation; the orchestrator changed that to add-on-every-write, so projects whose lock file already exists get the line too. test_relay_run now asserts a fully clean git status, with the lock filter removed. Counts: full suite 2003 OK (skipped=1); test_atomic 9, test_feedback 45 and test_relay_run 47 OK; slicer check passed (276 items); git diff --check clean.

trust: unverified; by: Jon Robbins

**Not in this slice:** removing the lock file after each write (it is an flock target and is meant to persist), and changing this repo's root `.gitignore`, which already ignores `/.slicer/lock` for itself.

## Why

`store.project_lock` (`src/slicer/store.py:178`) opens `.slicer/lock` with `O_CREAT` and never removes it. `init_project` (`src/slicer/ops.py:149`) adds only the feedback files to `.slicer/.gitignore` through `feedback.ensure_gitignore`. This repo hides the lock with its own root `.gitignore` (line 26), so the gap only shows in other projects: after the first `slicer add`, `git status` lists `.slicer/lock` as untracked. The s282 implementer hit it in a test repo on 2026-10-15.

## Files

- `src/slicer/ops.py`: `init_project` calls `feedback.ensure_gitignore(root, store.LOCK_NAME)` beside the feedback lines.
- `src/slicer/store.py`: in `project_lock`, when the lock file did not exist before `os.open`, add the line through `feedback.ensure_gitignore` (a function-level import, since `feedback` imports `store`). Plain file IO only; no git call.
- `tests/test_feedback.py` (the exact `.gitignore` assertions) and a new test class in `tests/test_store.py` or the nearest lock test module.
- `CHANGELOG.md`, and `docs/configuration.md` or `docs/getting-started.md` wherever the `.slicer/.gitignore` contents are described.
